stem: In this exposition line, what is 1395066363000?

options.text: An optional timestamp in milliseconds since the Unix epoch
options.note: Right. The third token is an optional int64 timestamp in milliseconds.
The value is 1027, the token right after the labels.

options.text: A timestamp in seconds since the Unix epoch
options.note: Exposition timestamps are in milliseconds, not seconds.
Series are identified by name and labels. There's no numeric series ID in the text format.

explanation: Sample lines have the form `metric_name{labels} value [timestamp]`. The timestamp is optional and is an int64 in milliseconds since the epoch.
hint: Count the digits. A 13-digit epoch number suggests a particular unit.

stem: A metric appears in a /metrics page with no # TYPE line. What type does it get?

options.note: Right. Without a TYPE line, the type is set to untyped.
There's no default to gauge. The format specifies untyped.
Not even if the name ends in _total. The default is untyped.
A missing TYPE line is allowed. It just means untyped.

explanation: If there is no TYPE line for a metric name, its type is set to untyped.
hint: There's a fifth type keyword besides the four metric types.

stem: Where must the # TYPE line for a metric appear?

options.text: Before the first sample of that metric
options.note: Right. The TYPE line must appear before the first sample reported for that metric name.
Position matters. It must come before the metric's first sample.
The opposite. It must come before them.

options.text: Only at the very top of the file
options.note: Each metric group has its own TYPE line, placed before that group's samples.

explanation: Only one TYPE line may exist per metric name, and it must appear before the first sample reported for that name.
hint: A parser needs to know the type before it reads the values.

stem: Which are valid types on a # TYPE line in the Prometheus text format? Select all that apply.

options.note: Right. One of the five valid type keywords.
Right. One of the five valid type keywords.
Right. It's also the default when no TYPE line is given.
Info is an OpenMetrics type, not a Prometheus text format type.
There's no timer type. Durations are usually histograms or summaries.

explanation: The TYPE line accepts counter, gauge, histogram, summary or untyped.
hint: Five keywords are valid: the four metric types plus one more.

stem: Which statement about a histogram in the text format is required by the format?

options.text: It must have a bucket with le="+Inf" whose value equals _count
options.note: Right. The format requires a +Inf bucket identical to x_count.

options.text: Its buckets must be in decreasing order of le
options.note: Buckets must appear in increasing numerical order of le.
_sum adds up the observed values. It's unrelated to the count.

options.text: It must not have a _sum line
options.note: Histograms expose a separate _sum sample.

explanation: A histogram must have a bucket with `{le="+Inf"}`, and its value must be identical to `x_count`. Buckets appear in increasing order of le.
hint: Cumulative buckets: which one holds everything?

stem: How is each quantile of a summary named x represented in the text format?

options.text: As a sample named x with a label quantile="y"
options.note: Right. Quantiles keep the base name and add a quantile label.
The quantile goes in a label, not in the metric name.

options.text: As a sample named x_bucket with a label le="y"
options.note: That's how histogram buckets are represented.

options.text: Quantiles aren't exposed. Only _sum and _count are
options.note: Summaries expose their quantiles as separate sample lines.

explanation: Each quantile of a summary named x is a separate sample line with the same name x and a label `{quantile="y"}`. Sum and count are x_sum and x_count.

stem: Which of these are rules of the Prometheus text format? Select all that apply.

options.text: All lines for a given metric must be provided as one single group
options.note: Right. A metric's lines can't be scattered through the page.

options.text: Each line must have a unique combination of metric name and labels
options.note: Right. Duplicates make ingestion behaviour undefined.

options.text: Lines must be sorted alphabetically by metric name
options.note: Reproducible sorting is preferred but not required.

options.text: Every line must include a timestamp
options.note: Timestamps are optional, as the minimalistic line in the example shows.

explanation: All lines for a metric must form one group (HELP and TYPE first), and each line must have a unique name+label combination. Sorting is preferred but optional, and timestamps are optional.
hint: Two are hard rules; two are things the format explicitly makes optional.

stem: Which of these are valid sample values in the text format? Select all that apply.

options.note: Right. NaN is a valid value.
Right. Positive infinity is valid.
Right. An ordinary float.
Values are floats. Strings aren't valid sample values.

explanation: Values are floats as parsed by Go's ParseFloat. NaN, +Inf and -Inf are also valid.
hint: Prometheus samples are always numeric, but some special float values exist.

stem: What is OpenMetrics, in relation to Prometheus?

options.text: A standardised exposition format built on the Prometheus text format, which Prometheus can scrape
options.note: Right. It grew out of the Prometheus text format and adds features such as exemplars and more types.

options.text: A replacement query language for PromQL
options.note: OpenMetrics is about exposing metrics on the wire, not querying them.
It's a format, not a storage system.
It's a format specification, not a library.

explanation: OpenMetrics is an effort to standardise metric wire formatting, built off the Prometheus text format. Prometheus can scrape it.
hint: It's about how metrics are written on the wire.

stem: Which of these is required in the OpenMetrics text format but not in the classic Prometheus text format?

options.text: The exposition must end with # EOF
options.note: Right. OpenMetrics text is trailed with # EOF.

options.text: Every sample must have a timestamp
options.note: Timestamps aren't required in either format.

options.text: Metric names must be all upper case
options.note: No such rule exists.

options.text: A # HELP line for every metric
options.note: HELP isn't the distinguishing requirement here.

explanation: The OpenMetrics text format uses UTF-8 with newline line endings and is trailed with `# EOF`.
hint: Think about how a parser knows the response is complete.

stem: Which Content-Type identifies the classic Prometheus text exposition format?

options.note: Right. That's the Content-Type for the Prometheus text format.
That one identifies the OpenMetrics text format.
Prometheus exposition isn't JSON.
YAML is used for configuration files, not exposition.

explanation: The Prometheus text format is served as `text/plain` with `version=0.0.4`. OpenMetrics uses `application/openmetrics-text`. Since 3.0, a missing or invalid Content-Type fails the scrape.
hint: The classic format is plain text.
